_description: Structural constants: values that shape the observation and action spaces, the module-ID naming contract, and the paths the visualizers read. These are real inputs - every module named by a _source key reads them through gym_continuousDoubleAuction/config_loader.py and holds no literal of its own. Per-run knobs live in train_config.json; env fallbacks live in env_defaults.json.
_note: Derived quantities are not listed. book_dim is book_rows * k_rows, snapshot_dim is book_dim + extra_dim, and the action space's price cardinality is k_rows. Writing a derived value here would create a second copy that can disagree with the first.

observation_layout._note: One observation snapshot is book_rows stacked rows of k_rows price levels - [bid_price, bid_size, ask_price, ask_size] - followed by extra_dim market-level scalars [log_mid, log1p_spread_ticks]. k_rows is the single definition of book depth: the observation exposes it, the action space's price code indexes it, and _set_price reshapes against it. book_rows is fixed by the four lists set_agg_LOB builds; changing it requires changing that function.

action_space._note: category_n is checked against the side/type mapping in _set_action_mkt_depth at construction, so a value that disagrees with that mapping raises instead of silently doing nothing. price_offset_n must be odd: the neutral 'join' code is the middle one, and offsets run from -(n//2) to +(n//2) ticks. The price code's cardinality is not here - it is observation_layout.k_rows.

price_anchor_fallbacks._note: Two fallbacks for the price anchor, both normally overwritten by reset(). action_helper_last_price seeds self.last_price before the first reset; state_helper_midpoint is used when the book has no two-sided market and last_price is unusable. They are read from one place now, so they cannot drift apart.

module_id_prefixes._note: A naming contract, not a knob: SelfPlayCallback parses these prefixes to tell baseline opponents from champion snapshots. Changing them invalidates existing checkpoints, whose module directories are named with the old prefix.

runtime_env_vars._note: Set with setdefault before ray.init, so an existing value in the environment wins. Add entries here rather than in code.

logging._note: How the package configures the standard library logging module, applied once per process by the first get_logger call. level is the fallback: $CDA_LOG_LEVEL wins over it, which is how the level reaches Ray's worker processes - they are separate interpreters that never run train.main, so train.py exports the variable and each worker's first import picks it up. env_var is named here so the exporter and the reader agree on one string. The format carries the pid because with num_env_runners > 0 every worker logs into the same stream, and without it the episode hooks are unattributable. It also carries iter=, the training iteration, so a log line can be joined to the progress.jsonl row for the same iteration; it reads '-' in any process that does not know the iteration, which is every env runner. datefmt carries the date because a training run outlasts a day and a time-only stamp cannot be ordered across midnight.
logging._file_note: The run log. Until this existed the package logged only to stdout, so the narrative a run is diagnosed from - the per-episode NAV tables, the league statistics, the ERROR that precedes a strict_nav_check raise - survived only in scrollback, while progress.jsonl kept the numbers. file_name is written under log_base_dir, beside progress.jsonl. Rotation bounds it: file_max_bytes per file, file_backup_count old files kept, so a long or resumed run cannot fill the disk. Set file_name to an empty string to disable file logging entirely.
logging._file_worker_note: Every process writes its own file rather than sharing one, because RotatingFileHandler is not safe across processes - two of them crossing the size threshold together rename and truncate the same file underneath each other. The driver writes file_name; a worker writes the same name with its pid before the suffix (run.log -> run.4231.log). This matters rather than being a detail: the episode callbacks run on the env runners, so with num_env_runners > 0 the NAV tables and the conservation ERROR are emitted there and nowhere else. dir_env_var carries log_base_dir to those workers the same way env_var carries the level - they are separate interpreters that never run train.main.

visualize_paths._note: Default arguments of the visualize entry points. The per-step record is Parquet, written by train.episode_record.EpisodeRecorder under <episode_parquet_dir>/<run_id>/ (train_config.json's episode_data_dir). episode_parquet_fallback is the path tried when episode_parquet_dir does not exist, which is what happens when the visualizer is run from inside visualize/. The visualizer picks the most recently modified run_id directory unless one is passed explicitly. training_log_dir/training_log_fallback are the same pattern for progress.jsonl, one per-iteration JSON line written under <training_log_dir>/<run_id>/ (train_config.json's log_base_dir).

inert_tick_size_copy._note: DOCUMENTATION ONLY - the one value in this file that is not read from here. OrderBook accepts and stores a tick_size it never reads, and the envs/orderbook/ package is off-limits to changes, so its literal default stays in that module. The live tick is Action_Helper.min_tick, which comes from the tick_size config key. Deleting the dead parameter is the documented recommendation (doc/15 S3-4). The env side of this is fixed: reset() now builds the book with the configured tick_size instead of a literal 1.
